facts.label: Field mapping error
facts.detail: Median distance between where vexvision and a hand-checked calibration put the same pixel, on 5 frames from 2 cameras the models never trained on.

facts.label: Match names read
facts.detail: Qual, elimination and final names read off the overlay on 83 frames; every miss was naming style ("Final 2" vs "Final 1-2").

facts.label: Team numbers read
facts.detail: Of the four teams named in each video title, on 332 team slots. With the event's team list, wrong reads drop out.

facts.label: Robot detector mAP50
facts.detail: On a camera it never trained on: a small test of 12 robots in 3 frames.

steps.title: Find the match
steps.text: Reads the overlay's match name and clock, then bisects a long livestream to the start of autonomous without downloading it.
steps.figure: Match names right on 94% of live frames

steps.title: Find goals and robots
steps.text: Two YOLO models trained on Override broadcast frames find the nine goals (by colour) and the robots.
steps.figure: Goals mAP50 0.54, robots 0.80, on unseen cameras

steps.title: Map the field
steps.text: Detected goals are matched to their known positions, the white tape snaps the fit into place, and a mirror check keeps the camera above the floor.
steps.figure: Median 1.2 in off on unseen cameras

steps.title: Follow four robots
steps.text: Exactly four tracks for the whole match. Alliance comes from the starting side of the Autonomous Line, so identities can't swap or multiply.

steps.title: Name the teams
steps.text: The schedule says which two teams are on each alliance, so naming is one yes-or-no per alliance, settled by licence-plate reads.
steps.figure: Misread plates like 2I45X still count for 2145X

steps.title: Read goals and Toggles
steps.text: Colour runs up each goal's stack become pin halves; the Toggle on each wall is read where it sits on the wall top.
steps.figure: Stack reading is a first heuristic, not yet measured

steps.title: Check the referees' score
steps.text: The running score on the broadcast and the official result show what the camera missed; seen and inferred points are kept apart.
steps.figure: Running score read on standard overlays

limits: Full-match tracking, placement and Toggle events and plate reading are built and tested on scripted data, but not yet measured on real match video.
Goal stacks are read by a colour heuristic until a goal close-up model is trained from hand counts (the labeling tool records them).
The models learned from a few hundred frames. Wide, whole-field camera angles work best; tight close-ups can't be mapped.
The screenshot tool runs the models in your browser; the first run downloads about 29 MB.
